title: App Router 15 — why are params and searchParams now Promises?
description: Next.js 15 makes route params async to support PPR and streaming — you must await them.
answer:
**TL;DR:** In Next.js 15, `params` and `searchParams` are Promises — you must `await` them in pages, layouts, and `generateMetadata` to unblock Partial Prerendering and streaming.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">Sync props (14) → Async Promise (15) → await + use()</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Next 14</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">params: {id} sync</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">blocking render</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">no PPR hole</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">Next 15</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">params: Promise<{id}></text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">searchParams: Promise</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">async opt-in</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Fix</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">await params</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">or use(params)</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">codemod: npx</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

Next.js 15 changes the App Router segment props: `params` and `searchParams` are no longer plain objects but Promises.

A page signature changes from `({ params })` to `({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> })`. This is not just an API annoyance — it lets Next.


| Area | Next 14 | Next 15 |
|---|---|---|
| `params` type | `{ id: string }` | `Promise<{ id: string }>` |
| `searchParams` | object | `Promise<object>` |
| How to read | `params.id` | `const { id } = await params` |

**Interview Tip:** In interviews, explain the why: Promises let Next render the static shell before resolving dynamic params, enabling PPR. Show both server `await` and client `use()` patterns.

```js
// app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx — Next 15
type Props = { params: Promise<{slug:string}>, searchParams: Promise<{q?:string}> };
export default async function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {
  const { slug } = await params;
  const { q } = await searchParams;
  const post = await db.post.findUnique({ where: { slug } });
  if (!post) notFound();
```

title: Turbopack — why is it 10x faster than Webpack in Next.js 15?
description: Turbopack is the Rust incremental bundler now stable for dev and gaining production support.

title: Migrating Webpack config to Turbopack — what breaks?
description: Moving custom Webpack loaders and aliases to Turbopack's `turbopack` config and compatibility shims.
answer:
**TL;DR:** Most `webpack:` customizations map to `experimental.turbo` or `turbopack` config; Turbopack handles SVGR, Sass, MDX natively but custom plugins that tap Webpack's compiler API still need Webpack.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">next.config webpack: → turbopack.rules + resolveAlias</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Webpack config</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">webpack:(c)=>modify</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">plugins tap API</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">loader chains</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">Turbopack compat</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">turbo.rules</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">resolveAlias</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">auto SVGR/Sass</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Fallback</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">webpack stays</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">next build still</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">prod fallback</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

When you switch `next dev` to Turbopack, your `next.config.js` `webpack: (config) => ...` hook is silently ignored — Turbopack does not run Webpack plugins.

For common cases (alias `@/*`, SVG as React component, Sass, YAML) Turbopack has first-class support via `experimental.turbo.rules` and `resolveAlias`/`resolveExtensions`. For example, an alias `webpack.resolve.alias['@ui']` becomes `experimental.turbo.resolveAlias['@ui']`.


| Custom piece | Webpack way | Turbopack way |
|---|---|---|
| Alias `@/*` | `config.resolve.alias` | `turbopack.resolveAlias` |
| SVG → React | `webpack rule + @svgr` | `turbo.rules['*.svg']` |
| Sass | automatic | automatic (native) |
| Compiler plugins | `config.plugins.push` | not supported — stay on Webpack |
| Analyzer | `webpack-bundle-analyzer` | `next experimental --turbo --analyze` |

**Interview Tip:** Interview angle: Turbopack is Rollup-style explicit rules, not Webpack plugin taps. Show you know to keep `webpack:` for prod fallback while `turbopack:` powers dev.

```js
// next.config.ts — dual config for incremental migration
const nextConfig = {
  turbopack: {
    rules: { '*.svg': { loaders: ['@svgr/webpack'], as: '*.js' } },
    resolveAlias: { '@ui': './src/ui' }
  },
  // kept for `next build` (Webpack) until turbo prod is GA
  webpack: (config) => {
    config.module.rules.push({ test: /\.svg$/, use: ['@svgr/webpack'] });
    return config;
  }
};
export default nextConfig;
```

title: What does `use cache` unlock in Next.js 15?
description: The new per-function cache directive that replaces manual `unstable_cache` and automatic fetch caching.
answer:
**TL;DR:** `'use cache'` marks an async function or component as cacheable — with `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` you control TTL and on-demand revalidation without wrapping fetch.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">'use cache' directive → cacheLife → cacheTag + revalidateTag</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">'use cache'</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">top of fn/component</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">makes result cacheable</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">replaces fetch cache</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">cacheLife</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">'minutes'|'hours'</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">TTL + stale</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">profile in config</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">cacheTag</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">cacheTag('posts')</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">revalidateTag()</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">on-demand purge</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

Next.js 15 introduces `'use cache'` (enabled via `experimental.cacheComponents: true` / `cacheComponents` in 15.2+).

Put `'use cache'` at the top of an async function, Server Component, or `server-only` module and its return value is cached (Data Cache + Full Route Cache when used inside a component).


| API | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `'use cache'` | top of async fn/component | opt into caching |
| `cacheLife(profile)` | inside cached fn | TTL (minutes/hours/custom) |
| `cacheTag(...tags)` | inside cached fn | tag for `revalidateTag` |

**Interview Tip:** Pitch it as React's `cache` + Next Data Cache unified: `'use cache'` is explicit, `cacheLife` is ISR TTL, `cacheTag` is on-demand ISR. Mention it will replace `fetch` caching heuristics.

```js
// app/lib/posts.ts — cached function with tags + TTL
'use cache';
import { cacheTag, cacheLife } from 'next/cache';

export async function getPost(slug: string) {
  'use cache';
  cacheLife('hours');          // revalidate ~1h
```

title: revalidateTag vs revalidatePath — when to use which?
description: Both do on-demand ISR but differ in granularity, cache keys, and Router Cache invalidation.
answer:
**TL;DR:** `revalidateTag` purges by Data Cache tag wherever it is used; `revalidatePath` purges a specific route — prefer tags for CMS content, path for page-centric invalidation.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">Mutation → revalidateTag (data) vs revalidatePath (route)</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">revalidateTag</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">tag: 'posts'</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">purges all fetch/'use cache'</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">granular, shared</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">revalidatePath</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">path: '/blog/[slug]'</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">purges Route Cache</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">page-centric</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Rule of thumb</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">CMS/data → tag</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">single page → path</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">call in Action</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

`revalidateTag(tag)` and `revalidatePath(path, type?)` both trigger on-demand revalidation, but they target different cache layers.

`revalidateTag` invalidates every Data Cache entry that was tagged with that string — whether via `fetch(...


| Aspect | `revalidateTag` | `revalidatePath` |
|---|---|---|
| Target | Data Cache by tag | Route Cache by path |
| Scope | everywhere tag used | single path (optionally `layout`) |
| Needs tagging | yes (`cacheTag`/`next.tags`) | no |
| Best for | shared CMS data | page-specific mutations |
| Next request | re-fetches tagged data | re-renders route |

**Interview Tip:** Answer template: tag is data-centric (purge by domain concept), path is URL-centric. For CMS say tag, for user-settings page say path. Mention both bust Router Cache.

```js
// app/actions/posts.ts — choose the right revalidation
'use server';
import { revalidateTag, revalidatePath } from 'next/cache';

export async function updatePost(slug: string, data: FormData) {
  await db.post.update({ where: { slug }, data: { title: data.get('title') as string } });
  revalidateTag('posts');               // all pages listing posts refresh
  revalidateTag(`post:${slug}`);        // detail cache for that slug
  revalidatePath(`/blog/${slug}`);      // ensure route + Router Cache bust
}
// For bulk publish webhook: only revalidateTag('posts') is enough
```

title: Parallel routes (@slot) — how do you build a dashboard with independent slots?

**TL;DR:** Parallel routes (`@slot` folders) let one layout render several `page.tsx` children at once — each slot has its own loading/error and navigates independently. title: next/font — how does it eliminate layout shift and external requests?
description: The built-in font optimizer self-hosts Google and local fonts, inlines fallbacks, and subsets glyphs at build.
answer:
**TL;DR:** `next/font` self-hosts fonts at build, inlines `size-adjust` fallback metrics and subsets, removing Google Fonts requests and CLS.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">Google Fonts CDN → next/font self-host + fallback metrics → 0 CLS</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Before</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5"><link href=google></text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">external RTT</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">CLS flash</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">next/font</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">auto self-host</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">subset + preload</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">size-adjust CSS</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Result</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">no external req</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">CLS 0</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">privacy + speed</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

`next/font/google` and `next/font/local` run at build time: they download the font files, generate subsets (latin, latin-ext, etc.), emit them as static assets with hashed names, and inject `@font-face` with `font-display: optional/swap` plus automatically calculated `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, and `descent-override` so the fallback font matches metrics and no layout shift occurs.

No `<link>` to `fonts.googleapis.com` is needed — fonts are served from your domain/CDN, improving privacy and removing a render-blocking request. Usage is a function call that returns `className` and `variable` (for CSS variables with `variable` fonts).


| Aspect | `<link>` Google Fonts | `next/font` |
|---|---|---|
| Requests | 2-3 external | 0 (self-hosted) |
| Fallback | system font jump → CLS | `size-adjust` → 0 CLS |
| Privacy | Google sees IP | no third party |
| Subsetting | manual | automatic at build |
| Variable fonts | manual CSS | `variable: '--font-...'` |

**Interview Tip:** Mention `size-adjust` fallback metrics: that is the clever bit interviewers want. Also note self-hosting eliminates the extra RTT.

```js
// app/layout.tsx
import { Inter, JetBrains_Mono } from 'next/font/google';
import localFont from 'next/font/local';
const inter = Inter({ subsets:['latin'], display:'swap', variable:'--font-inter' });
const geist = localFont({ src:'./fonts/Geist.woff2', display:'swap', variable:'--font-geist' });
export default function RootLayout({children}:{children:React.ReactNode}){
  return <html lang="en" className={`${inter.variable} ${geist.variable}`}><body>{children}</body></html>;
}
```

title: Middleware in Next 15 — what breaks from the 14 upgrade?
description: Middleware now runs on the Node runtime option, `request` is async, and matching semantics tightened.
answer:
**TL;DR:** Next 15 middleware keeps Edge by default but now supports `runtime: 'nodejs'`, async `NextRequest` helpers, and `instrumentation` sharing — update matchers and await `request` APIs.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">Request → middleware (edge|node) → rewrite/redirect → RSC render</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Edge (default)</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">global low latency</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">no Node fs</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">auth + geo</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">Node option</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">runtime: 'nodejs'</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">full Node APIs</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">DB inside middleware</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Breaking</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">await request.*</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">matcher strict</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">no unstable_</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

Middleware (`middleware.ts` at root or `src/middleware.ts`) still runs before every matched route.

In Next 15 the headline changes: you can now opt a middleware into the Node runtime (`export const config = { runtime: 'nodejs' }` — previously Edge-only), so you can use Node `crypto`, `fs` (carefully) or ORM reads without splitting to a Route Handler.


| Area | Next 14 | Next 15 |
|---|---|---|
| Runtimes | Edge only | Edge (default) + Node opt-in |
| Request helpers | sync | now async-aware (await where needed) |
| Matcher | loose exclude | strict — verify `_next` bypass |

**Interview Tip:** Say: middleware is for fast redirect/rewrite and auth gating, not heavy DB. Highlight the new Node runtime option as the key 15 change.

```js
// middleware.ts — Next 15 (Edge by default, Node opt-in)
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server';
export async function middleware(req: NextRequest){
  const token = req.cookies.get('session')?.value;
  const isAuth = req.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith('/dashboard');
  if (isAuth && !token) return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', req.url));
```

title: Server Components and external packages — what does `serverComponentsExternalPackages` do?
description: Control which Node packages stay external to the Server Component bundle and run with native APIs.
answer:
**TL;DR:** `serverComponentsExternalPackages` tells Next not to bundle heavy/native Node packages into the RSC graph — they run as external Node requires, fixing native addon errors.

<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">tree-shaken</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">fast cold</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">External</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">sharp, prisma, pg</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">native binary</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">require at runtime</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Config</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">serverComponentsExternal</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">array of names</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">no client bundle</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>

Server Components run in Node, but Next still bundles their dependency graph to optimize and trace imports.

Packages with native binaries (`sharp`, `prisma`, `bcrypt`, `pg`, `canvas`, `puppeteer`) or that do dynamic `require()` break when bundled — you see errors like `Module not found: Can't resolve 'sharp'` or `prisma is not a function`. Listing them in `next.config.js` under `experimental.


| Package type | Bundle? | Example | Symptom if bundled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pure JS (zod, date-fns) | yes | `zod` | fine |
| Native binary | external | `sharp` | `Cannot find module sharp` |
| ORM client | external | `prisma` | runtime init fails |
| Mixed (needs both) | external server, bundle client | `react-pdf` | SSR crash |

**Interview Tip:** Name-drop `sharp` and `prisma` as canonical examples. Explain the fix is keeping native requires external so Node loads the binary at runtime.

```js
// next.config.ts — keep native packages external to RSC bundle
const nextConfig = {
  // Next 15 stable key (fallback: experimental.serverComponentsExternalPackages)
  serverExternalPackages: ['sharp', 'prisma', '@prisma/client', 'bcrypt'],
};
export default nextConfig;
// app/api/image/route.ts — can now use sharp safely
import sharp from 'sharp';
export async function GET(){ const buf = await sharp('./photo.jpg').resize(800).toBuffer(); return new Response(buf,{headers:{'Content-Type':'image/jpeg'}}); }
```

title: next.config `reactCompiler` — should you enable the React Compiler?
description: The `reactCompiler: true` flag auto-memoizes components, replacing manual `useMemo`/`useCallback`.
answer:
**TL;DR:** Setting `reactCompiler: true` in `next.config.js` runs the React Compiler (Forget) at build — it auto-inserts memoization so you can remove most `useMemo`/`useCallback`.

<svg class="iq-diagram" viewBox="0 0 820 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="16" y="18" font-size="11">Manual memo → React Compiler (build) → auto memo slots</text>
<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#22c55e" stroke="#22c55e"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Before</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">useMemo/useCallback</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">deps arrays</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">missed memo bugs</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#f59e0b" stroke="#f59e0b"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">Compiler</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">Babel/SWC pass</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">analyzes reactivity</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">inserts cache slots</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Next flag</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">reactCompiler:true</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">eslint plugin</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">bailout warnings</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

The React Compiler (formerly React Forget) is a build-time transform that automatically memoizes computations and callbacks.

In Next.js 15 you enable it with `reactCompiler: true` in `next.config.js` (or `experimental.reactCompiler` in older 15).


| Aspect | Without compiler | With `reactCompiler: true` |
|---|---|---|
| Memoization | manual `useMemo`/`useCallback` | auto inserted |
| Dependency lists | you maintain | compiler infers |
| Bailout cause | — | mutation, global read, incompatible hook |
| ESLint | no signal | `react-compiler` warnings |
| Bundle impact | smaller (hand-tuned) | small runtime cache (~1-2KB) |

**Interview Tip:** Interview kicker: the compiler is opt-in via next.config and requires eslint fixes for bailouts — never promise it memoizes everything.

```js
// next.config.ts — enable React Compiler
const nextConfig = {
  reactCompiler: true, // Next 15 stable
  // optional: eslint already warns via eslint-config-next
};
export default nextConfig;
// Before: const onClick = useCallback(()=>doExpensive(a),[a]);
// After (with compiler): plain function is memoized automatically
function Button({ a }: {a:number}){
  const onClick = () => doExpensive(a); // compiler caches
  return <button onClick={onClick}>go</button>;
}
```

A key Next 15 migration surprise: `fetch()` calls without an explicit cache option and `export async function GET()` Route Handlers are now **uncached** (dynamic) by default.

In Next 14, `fetch('https://api...


| API | Next 14 default | Next 15 default | To cache again |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fetch(url)` | `force-cache` | `no-store` (dynamic) | `fetch(url,{ cache:'force-cache'})` or `'use cache'` |
| `GET` Route Handler | static | dynamic | `export const dynamic='force-static'` |
| `unstable_cache` | n/a | same | add `revalidate`/`tags` |
| `'use cache'` fn | n/a | opt-in cached | `cacheLife` + `cacheTag` |

**Interview Tip:** Flag the upgrade gotcha: fetch/GET went from cached to dynamic. Show you know the fix is `cache:'force-cache'` or `'use cache'` for CMS paths.

```js
// Next 15 — opt back into caching where stale is OK
// 1) fetch with revalidate
const res = await fetch('https://cms.example/posts', { next: { revalidate: 3600, tags:['posts'] } });
// 2) make a GET handler static again
// app/api/revalidate/route.ts
export const dynamic = 'force-static';
export const revalidate = 600;
export async function GET(){ return Response.json({ time: Date.now() }); }
// 3) DB via 'use cache'
// export async function getPosts(){ 'use cache'; cacheLife('hours'); cacheTag('posts'); return db.post.findMany(); }
```

title: PPR vs ISR vs SSR — how do you pick the rendering strategy in Next 15?
description: Decision matrix for static, ISR, SSR, and PPR — covering freshness, TTFB, and CDN costs.
answer:
**TL;DR:** Use PPR for mixed pages (static shell + personalized holes), ISR for time-based revalidation, SSR/dynamic for fully per-request data — PPR gives CDN speed with per-request holes.

In Next 15 the choice is not binary static vs dynamic — PPR sits in the middle.

Use **Static/ISR** (`export const revalidate = 60` or `'use cache'` with `cacheLife`) when freshness tolerance is minutes/hours and the whole page can share one TTL (blog posts, product catalog). TTFB is CDN-fast, cost is low, but data is stale until revalidation.

| PPR | `ppr:'incremental'` + `Suspense` | fast (shell CDN) | per-hole fresh | medium | PDP, feed |
